name: Record page
description: The screen for one record: the band that identifies it and says what state it is in, a strip of the figures that matter, and the sections of detail below it — line items, approvals, documents, activity — carrying only the actions the record's current state allows.
when_to_use: One record opened to be read and then decided on — PO-2026-0418, GRN-4821, a vendor, an indent. The line against form-page is the reason the reader came: they came to change the record, so form-page, and its readonly variant is that same edit screen showing its own fields in read mode while nobody is editing; they came to read the record and then decide, so this. It is not a form with the inputs turned off. The figures are summarised rather than listed field by field, the line items are a table with a total rather than an editable grid, and half of this page is regions a form does not have at all — the approval trail, the documents, the activity, the linked records. A record with four facts and no sections is form-page/readonly, and building it here is ceremony. page-header is the top block of this page and not the page: reach for page-header when the band on its own is what you are placing, over a register or over a form, and reach for this when the band plus the summary plus the sections is the screen. tabs is the switching mechanism the tabs variant here uses and it is a component rather than a layout — a tab row over something that is not one record is tabs and not this. And where the next record matters as much as this one — a QC hold queue, an approval run somebody clears before the shift ends — the screen is list-detail, because there the queue never leaves the screen; a record page is what you open when you arrived from a register and the register can wait. The register itself is data-table.
rules: This renders inside app-shell, as the whole of <main>. The band and the body share one gutter and that is the only thing they have to agree on: it is written here as mx-auto max-w-6xl because a record reads better bounded than a register does, and if the application uses the register gutter of max-w-[1600px] then both the band and the body take that instead. Mismatch them and the h1 sits a few pixels off the first card.

The summary strip is card/stats' divided footer, not a row of stat-cards. A record's figures are parts of one total — ordered, received, invoiced, balance — and they add up, which is exactly what four independent tiles with gaps between them say they do not. stat-card also carries a delta, and a single record has no previous period to compare against, so three quarters of that component would be drawn empty.

Sections are stacked down the page until there are enough of them to be worth switching. Stacked, the whole record prints in one pass, Ctrl+F finds all of it, and nobody has to remember which tab the GRN was under. Tabs earn their place past about four sections or where one of them is expensive to render, and then the tabs variant is the shape — never both, because a page with three stacked sections and a tab row over two more has no answer to where anything is.

Line items are table's markup unchanged: the same header cells, the same tabular-nums and text-right on the figures, the same total in a <tfoot>, and the same stacked cards below md. The one thing this page adds is that the table is read-only. A record page that makes its lines editable has become form-page/line-items wearing the wrong header, and the two then disagree about what a line is.

An action the state has removed is gone, not disabled. A disabled Record GRN on a cancelled order is a dead Tab stop that explains nothing and invites the press it will refuse; the banner is what carries the reason, and the button is simply not drawn. Disable a control only while its own request is in flight — that is the case where the control still exists.

Cancelled and On hold are not in the locked five, and there is no sixth dot. On hold takes Approved's amber-500, because its meaning is exactly the one amber has: waiting on someone. Cancelled takes Draft's zinc-400, the inert shade: the record is over, and neither of the other candidates says that. Emerald would say it finished well, and zinc-500 would say it is still live. Both words are in the status table now — this entry was written before they were, and reached the same two answers on its own.

The rail here is first in the DOM and placed second by the grid, which is the reverse of form-page/side-rail. The reason that entry puts its rail last is that the rail is context beside a form the user is filling, and the tab order should be the form and then the context. This rail is the record's identity and standing, it is what a phone reader wants above the lines rather than below them, and it holds nothing focusable at all — so there is no tab order to get wrong, and lg:col-start-2 lg:row-start-1 is free. Put one control in it and that stops being true; move the control into the page.

One h1 and it is the record's own identity — the order number, the vendor's name, the batch code. Not "Purchase order", which names the register this came from and is the same string on 1,438 pages. Everything below the band is h2, and a subsection inside a section is h3.

A deep link to a tab selects that panel and does not move focus. The page has just loaded, so the browser is already at the top of the document and the reader has not asked to be anywhere else; pulling focus into the panel at boot skips the band that says which record they are looking at. Focus moves on a tab the reader pressed, and on nothing else.

A figure the reader may not see is absent, not blanked. No dots, no em dash, no disabled column toggle — the Rate and Value columns are simply not in the table, the money cells are not in the summary strip, and one sentence under the table says which scope is closed and who opens it. A blanked cell is a claim that there is a number there and you are not important enough for it, which is the same information leak wearing a courtesy.

A before-and-after in the activity trail needs words as well as the strike-through. line-through is announced by some screen readers as deleted text and by most as nothing at all, so the old value is followed by an sr-only "changed to" and the arrow is decorative. Without it the entry reads as "Promised delivery 02 Aug 2026 22 Aug 2026", which is two dates and no direction.

On a record that is with the reader for approval, the approval section moves to the top and the decision lives inside it. An Approve button in the band is pressed before the record has been read — it is the first thing the eye lands on and it is one press from done. Beside the trail it is one press from done only after the reader has scrolled past who has already signed and why.

anatomy.description: page-header's record variant unchanged: a <header> inside <main>, white, edge to edge over a border-zinc-200 rule, holding the breadcrumb, the one h1, the status pill and the actions. Never overflow-hidden — the action menu opens out of the bottom of it.

badge's locked pill beside the title, and the qualifier that says why anybody cares — "4 of 9 lines received" — outside the shape, because a pill that grows to a phrase stops matching the column this record occupies on the register.

One white panel divided into two to four cells, each a term and a figure: what was ordered, what has arrived, what has been billed, what is left. Two columns below sm and four from sm up, with the rules drawn as borders on the cells rather than by divide-x, which puts a rule down the left edge of the third cell the moment the grid wraps.
A card per region, h2 in its header, and the header carries the count and the one action that belongs to that region. Cards are the sections and dividers are the subsections; they do not nest.
table's markup inside a card with no body padding, the total in a <tfoot>, and the same rows as stacked cards below md. Read-only.

An <ol> on marker's rail: who signed, when, who it is with now, and who has not been reached yet. The rail stays zinc-200 the whole way down — colouring the part above the current step turns it into a progress bar whose total is written nowhere.
attachment's list in read mode: type, name, size, who attached it and when, and Download without Remove. A control that cannot act is a control that should not be drawn.
The audit region, newest first, grouped by day under an h3 per day, with the changed fields shown as an old value and a new one.

The indents, receipts and invoices hanging off this one, as a wrapped list of real links. This is the region that has no equivalent on a form and the commonest reason somebody opens the record at all.
alert's neutral card above the sections when the state needs explaining — cancelled, on hold, superseded. White, zinc border, colour only in the icon, and it says who did it and when.
The cluster in the band, ordered so the primary is last, holding only what this state allows. What the state has removed is absent rather than disabled.

behaviour: The band does not stick. On a record long enough that the actions leave the screen, the phone arrangement puts them in a bar at the foot and the desktop one repeats nothing — a record is read top to bottom and the decision is taken at the end of it.

The summary strip restacks from four cells to two below sm and never scrolls sideways. The figures are tabular-nums, so a receipt posted against the record does not change the width of the column it sits in.

Line items scroll with the page. The table becomes stacked cards below md carrying the same fields in the same order, and the total is repeated as a strip under them rather than dropped — the total is why the screen was opened.

Switching tabs changes the panel and nothing above it. The breadcrumb, the h1, the status and the summary strip are the record, not a view of it, so they stay put; the tab id is written into the query string with replaceState, so a reload lands on the same panel and Back leaves the record rather than undoing a tab.

A record that is awaiting the reader's own approval reorders: the approval section comes first, its current step is expanded, and the decision controls are inside it. Every other reader sees the same section in its ordinary place, closed, with no controls in it.

Actions follow the state. Cancelled keeps Print and Duplicate and loses Amend and Record GRN entirely; on hold keeps Release hold and loses Amend; closed keeps Print and Duplicate. Nothing is drawn disabled and nothing is drawn that the server would refuse.

A field the account may not read is not rendered — no column, no cell, no placeholder — and the sentence under the region says which scope is closed and who grants it. The rest of the record renders normally; a permission on one field does not blank the page.

Activity is newest first and grouped by day. Field changes carry the old value and the new one; entries older than the retained window are a link to the archive rather than an endless scroller on a record page.

At 390px the rail and the tab row both become something else: the rail's facts fold into the band's definition list and the summary strip, and the tab row becomes a native select with each section a real <section> and no tab roles anywhere.
accessibility: One <main>, one <h1> in the band, every section an h2 and every day heading in the activity trail an h3. The heading outline is how somebody skims a record they did not open, and on this page it is the only navigation there is.

The band is a <header> inside <main>, which makes it a section header rather than the banner landmark. The banner belongs to the shell's topbar, and a second one gives a landmark list nobody can navigate.

The breadcrumb is a <nav aria-label="Breadcrumb"> with aria-current="page" on the last crumb, which is a <span> and not a link. Its name differs from the sidebar's, or the landmark list holds two identical rows.

The status pill carries the word as well as the dot, and the dot is aria-hidden. A pill whose only content is colour is an empty element to a screen reader and an unreadable one to anybody who cannot separate red from grey.

Where tabs are used they carry the whole pattern from tabs — role="tablist" with a name, aria-selected and aria-controls out, aria-labelledby back, roving tabindex, and arrow, Home and End all preventing default. A row of styled buttons promises that arrows switch panels and then nothing does.

The summary strip is a <dl>: a figure with a heading above it is two paragraphs that happen to be adjacent, and read on its own "₹8,16,400" is a number with no word attached to it. Two <dd> under one <dt> is how the figure and its qualifier stay one unit.
A before-and-after in the activity trail says "changed to" in sr-only text between the two values. The strike-through and the arrow are decoration and neither of them is a direction.
The approval trail is an <ol> because the order is the record, not the layout, and every mark in the rail column is aria-hidden — the dates and the words are what say who signed and when.
The permission sentence is prose in the region it applies to, not a title attribute and not a disabled control. There is nothing to hover on a phone, and a dead Tab stop explains nothing.

At 390px the section select is a real <select> with a real label and no tab roles at all, and each section is a <section> with its own heading. Giving a select role="tab" breaks the one thing it was brought in to do.
